feedback: If you cannot explain why l × w gives area: rebuild the array — each row has 'length' squares and there are 'width' rows, so the total squares = length × width.
If a missing side is wrong: check with the array (does your width, times the length, give the stated area?) or substitute back into your equation.
Always re-check units at the end: a surface answer is square units, an around-the-edge answer is linear units.
activities.intendedInsight: The area formula is a shortcut for counting rows × columns of unit squares, and a missing side can be found by reasoning backwards from the area (or as an equation), while perimeter adds the edge lengths.
learnerActions: Cover a labelled rectangle with unit-square tiles (or draw the array on squared paper) and count the squares by rows × columns to see where length × width comes from.
Compute the perimeter of the same rectangle as 2 × (length + width), and label each answer with its unit (cm² for area, cm for perimeter).
Find a missing dimension: given area 48 m² and length 8 m, work back to width 6 m; calculate the area of a square with side 7.5 cm (56.25 cm²).
Write a missing-measure problem as an equation, e.g. 4 + 2b = 20, and solve for b.
activities.title: Build l × w from an array of unit squares, then express a missing side algebraically

feedback: If a units item is wrong, send the learner back to the meaning: area counts covering squares (square units); perimeter measures distance (linear units).

If the blob estimate ignores part-squares or counts every touched square whole, remind them of the agreed part-square rule (either 'at least half counts as one' or pairing part-squares into about one whole) and to apply it consistently.
If area and perimeter are swapped, re-link each formula to its meaning before retrying.
activities.intendedInsight: Confirm that the learner can apply both formulae accurately, choose correct units, and estimate an irregular area.
learnerActions: Compute the area and the perimeter of a labelled rectangle, then answer a units question (is the area cm or cm²?).
Find a missing width when given the area and the length.
Estimate the area of a gridded blob, including part-squares.
activities.title: Checking quiz: area, perimeter, missing side and estimate with a units check
